description: Native 2x scaling for maximum FPS. Use Proteus v4 (never Rhea for 1080p→4K).
use_case: Quick upscales from 1080p video to 4K with maximum throughput and minimal latency

improve_detail.tooltip: Moderate detail injection. Proteus is conservative.

sharpen.tooltip: Push this on clean footage to prevent soft upscale.

anti_alias_deblur.tooltip: Negative = anti-aliasing. Tighten 1080p aliasing before 4K scaling.

recover_original_detail.tooltip: High blend—preserve 1080p micro-contrast and film grain.

add_noise_amount.tooltip: Add 16mm-style grain to break up AI smoothness.

gpu_optimization.note: CPU Grain is a bottleneck. Use prenoise (GPU) instead.

ffmpeg_cli: ffmpeg -hide_banner -i "input_1080p.mp4" -sws_flags spline+accurate_rnd+full_chroma_int -filter_complex "tvai_up=model=prob-4:scale=2:preblur=-0.15:noise=0.10:details=0.35:halo=0.05:blur=0.30:compression=0.25:prenoise=0.002:blend=0.50:device=0:vram=0.85:instances=1" -c:v hevc_nvenc -profile:v main10 -pix_fmt p010le -rc constqp -qp 16 -preset p6 -c:a copy "output_4k.mp4"
why_not_rhea: Rhea has only a native 4x model. When you ask it to upscale 1080p→4K (2x), Topaz internally upscales to 8K then downscales to 4K. This tanks FPS to 2-4 and wastes VRAM.
why_focus_fix_off: Focus Fix forces an internal downscale+4x upscale penalty. For clean 1080p, it's unnecessary overhead.
common_mistakes: Using Rhea instead of Proteus (causes terrible FPS)
Enabling Focus Fix (adds 18% latency for no benefit)
Setting Max Memory to 100% (CUDA OOM crash)
Running 2+ parallel processes on 1 job (PCIe thrash)
expected_output: Crisp 4K (3840x2160) @ 60fps, sharp details, no plastic skin, preserved film grain, no artifacts

testing.step_1: Render 30 seconds on a fast GPU (RTX 4070+)
testing.step_2: Check FPS in Topaz UI (should be 15+ FPS)
testing.step_3: Play output in VLC—look for aliasing, banding, or hallucinations
testing.step_4: If you see 'plastic skin' or 'swimming' textures, lower Improve Detail to 30
